headline: Dry high pressure brings sunny afternoons, chilly Kentucky nights and a clearing, breezy Upstate
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Continental high pressure controls the weather through Tuesday before shifting east and allowing a modest Wednesday warm-up. Sunshine, low humidity and no meaningful rain chance dominate. Clear skies favor efficient nighttime cooling, and the verified KDVK and KLEX cold biases support lower and wider overnight ranges than unadjusted guidance.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS alerts; a few sheltered valleys may reach the upper 30s overnight, but frost is unlikely
days.forecast: Sunny and dry with northeast winds around 5–8 mph. Afternoon temperatures reach the lower to middle 70s. Clear skies continue tonight; most locations fall into the lower 40s, while protected rural valleys may briefly reach the upper 30s. The range is shifted colder to account for the documented KDVK and KLEX nighttime biases.

days.label: Tuesday
days.forecast: Sunny and seasonably mild with a light east wind near 5–7 mph. HRRR, RAP, NAM and the NWS forecast favor the lower or middle 70s; warmer GFS guidance supports the upper end of the range. Tuesday night remains clear and cool, with the coldest rural sites near the lower 40s.

days.label: Wednesday
days.forecast: Sunny and warmer as surface flow turns southwesterly. Highs rebound toward 80, with the warmer global guidance allowing lower 80s. Wednesday night is clear and less chilly than the previous two nights, although rural valleys remain several degrees cooler than Lexington.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky stays sunny and rain-free through Wednesday. The main forecast detail is tonight's strong radiational cooling, including locally upper-30s temperatures in sheltered valleys; afternoon warmth then builds back toward 80 on Wednesday.
kentucky.confidence: High on dry weather and clear nights; high on Monday and Tuesday temperatures; moderate-high on Wednesday's exact high because the global models are warmer than NAM and the NWS point forecast

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: Patchy morning fog and low cloud lift by late morning, followed by a dry three-day stretch under high pressure. A cool northeast breeze holds Tuesday slightly below normal before sunshine and lighter winds allow a Wednesday warm-up. Official KCEU and KLQK observations—not Tempest data—anchor the forecast and later verification.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS alerts; patchy morning fog and low ceilings may briefly reduce visibility
days.forecast: Patchy fog and low cloud around Clemson and Central lift by late morning, followed by a dry afternoon with increasing sunshine. Light east-northeast winds and the slower morning clearing may hold some locations in the middle 70s, while sunnier locations approach the upper 70s. Tonight is mostly clear and cooler, with sheltered KLQK-area pockets near 50.

days.label: Tuesday
days.hazard: Northeast gusts near 18 mph are possible during the afternoon
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and a little cooler under renewed northeast flow. Winds increase to about 6–10 mph with occasional gusts near 18 mph. The NWS, HRRR, RAP and NAM favor lower or middle 70s, while the GFS is warmer, so the range stays wider than normal. Clear and cool conditions follow Tuesday night.

days.label: Wednesday
days.forecast: Sunny with lighter east winds and a modest warm-up. NAM and the NWS keep highs mainly in the upper 70s, while GFS and ECMWF support localized lower 80s. Wednesday night remains mostly clear; the lower edge of the low-temperature range retains the verified KLQK cold-pocket tendency.

upstate.bottomLine: Morning fog and low cloud are the only near-term concern. The Upstate turns sunny and remains dry through Wednesday, with a breezy, slightly cooler Tuesday followed by a warmer Wednesday. No official NWS alerts were active at issuance.
upstate.confidence: High on dry weather after morning fog clears; moderate-high on daily highs because morning cloud erosion and Tuesday northeast flow create a few degrees of uncertainty

sourceNotes: Official airport observations span 8:15–8:30 AM EDT. The NWS point forecasts were generated at approximately 8:58 AM EDT; the Kentucky grid was updated at 4:36 AM EDT and the Upstate grid at 6:20 AM EDT.

The Louisville and Greenville-Spartanburg Area Forecast Discussions were issued at 6:35 AM and 6:34 AM EDT. Louisville supports dry weather, middle-70s highs through Tuesday, locally upper-30s readings tonight and a Wednesday warm-up. Greenville-Spartanburg expects patchy fog and low cloud to lift by late morning, followed by dry weather through Friday and a slightly cooler Tuesday.

The NWS active-alert API returned no active alerts for either forecast point at the approximately 8:45 AM EDT check. This official alert status is separate from the independent discussion of patchy fog, reduced visibility and locally chilly valley temperatures.

Model inventories checked at 8:50 AM EDT showed the complete 06Z HRRR through hour 48, complete 09Z RAP through hour 51, 06Z NAM through hour 84, 06Z NAM 3-km Nest through hour 60, 06Z GFS and GEFS mean through hour 384, and 06Z ECMWF through hour 144. Partial newer cycles were not substituted for complete cycles beyond their available ranges.

College of DuPage NEXLAB radar at 8:40 AM EDT showed no meaningful precipitation over Central Kentucky or the Clemson area. Clean-infrared imagery at 8:41 AM EDT supported clear Kentucky skies and residual cloud cover over parts of the Carolinas, consistent with the observed Upstate fog and low cloud.

The College of DuPage model panels cluster around lower-to-middle-70s temperatures Tuesday, apart from a warmer GFS solution. For Wednesday, NAM and the NWS remain near the upper 70s while GFS and ECMWF support lower 80s. The forecast ranges retain both credible clusters, with ECMWF given less weight because its current scored sample is small and includes a larger prior error.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.

The forecast-accuracy summary generated at 4:09 PM EDT October 4 was consulted. KDVK and KLEX overnight ranges were shifted approximately 2–2.5°F lower. Upstate nighttime ranges were widened downward for KLQK's verified cold-pocket bias without imposing the full 4°F correction on KCEU and Clemson. Day-one and day-three ranges were widened because verified coverage at 24 and 72 hours remains below 50%, and small residual precipitation probabilities were retained because the 0–20% bin has observed precipitation slightly more often than forecast.
Radar, satellite and model-image links are timestamped external references. This candidate does not modify the repository, forecast archive, website or widget.

appliedAdjustments.details: Shifted overnight ranges roughly 2–2.5°F lower using the verified KDVK and KLEX low-temperature corrections. Kept daytime ranges centered on current guidance because station high-temperature biases remain below the correction threshold, and widened the day-one and day-three ranges because 24- and 72-hour coverage remains below 50%.

Widened nighttime ranges downward to represent KLQK's verified cold-pocket bias without imposing the full 4°F correction across Clemson and KCEU. Retained wider Tuesday and Wednesday high ranges to represent the model spread and down-weighted the warmer ECMWF solution because its current score is based on only two cases and has the largest error.
